text:
mike_supp: FYI large customer (tenant: acme-corp) reporting a spike of 502/504s hitting hosted inference since ~11:23 PDT. Only affects batched embeddings endpoint (/v1/embeddings:batch). Sample trace IDs: t-8bd3, t-8bd4, t-8bd9. We have a customer repro curl and one captured envoy stream reset.

javier_support: can you paste the minimal repro curl and the trace id that matches an envoy log?

mike_supp: here's the repro we gave them:```curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/embeddings:batch \n-H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED' \n-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n-d '{"model":"embed-ctxt-16k","inputs":["a lot of text...","another doc..."],"tenant":"acme-corp","metadata":{"x-tenant-meta":"az=west,env=prod"}}'```
Trace: t-8bd3 -> envoy: `stream reset, reason: connection failure (RST_STREAM)` in the same minute.

ash_prodeng: quick notes: 1) this customer uses large batch sizes with long seq lengths; 2) they recently rolled a client-side header `x-tenant-meta` that sometimes is ~8kb when combined with other metadata; 3) only acme-corp tenants hitting the embeds batch path are impacted (other routes OK).

sophie_sre: @ash_prodeng thanks. I'm seeing a correlation in edge metrics: per-tenant concurrent streams for acme-corp jumped from ~12 -> ~120 at 11:22 and h2 connection window exhaustion + GOAWAYs increased. Envoy log snippet:```[2026-03-15T18:11:23.456Z] cluster: upstream reset: rst_stream (0x1) stream_id=4251, flags=0x0, reason=STREAM_IDLE
[2026-03-15T18:11:23.457Z] connection: HTTP/2 window exceeded, sending GOAWAY last_stream_id=1024 error_code=ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM
[2026-03-15T18:11:23.458Z] stream: downstream reset due to 2 upstream resets```

lindsey_pm: customer says errors started right after they turned on metadata enrichment (adds headers) and increased batch size. They want a workaround asap.

javier_support: immediate mitigation options: 1) suggest temporary reduce batch size to 8; 2) ask them to stop sending large metadata headers; 3) we can throttle tenant at edge (rate-limit rule) to smooth bursts. Which is quickest for them?

mike_supp: told them to drop batch -> 8 and remove metadata header for now. They responded that reducing batch helped but still occasional 502s on long requests (~>8s).

ash_prodeng: that fits a different failure mode: long-lived streams + insufficient h2 stream window causing mid-stream resets when KV cache/serving side takes longer. Two follow-ups to repro: 1) can someone capture a full tcpdump + envoy access log for a failing stream; 2) capture a hostedapi request/response trace (we have tracing on for this tenant).

opsbot: Deploy bot: new canary config applied to edge-proxy group at 18:05 UTC (no config touching h2 windows).

sophie_sre: I grabbed access logs for t-8bd3 and t-8bd9. Access log summary:```remote=1.2.3.4 method=POST path=/v1/embeddings:batch status=502 upstream_code=RST_STREAM duration_ms=8123 resp_bytes=0 tenant=acme-corp batch_size=16 seq_len_avg=6400 headers_size=8120```
Full header dump shows `x-tenant-meta` at ~7.9kb.

ash_prodeng: interesting — headers_size > typical, and duration ~8s. When upstream (model runtime) takes >7s we hit proxy-level timeouts/stream resets depending on conn/window settings. Can we check our envoy config: `upstream_flush_timeout`, `stream_idle_timeout`, and HTTP/2 initial window size?

ash_prodeng: current values (from config): `stream_idle_timeout: 30s`, `upstream_flush_timeout: 6s`, `http2_initial_window: 65535`

javier_support: upstream_flush_timeout 6s looks suspicious given model latency >8s. That would cause Envoy to close the upstream stream while downstream still waiting -> 502s. Suggest increasing upstream_flush_timeout to 20s for this tenant route or set a per-route override for embeds.

sophie_sre: agree. But side effect: raising flush timeout keeps connections open longer which can increase h2 stream concurrency pressure. For acme-corp their burst concurrency already saturated. Two-pronged mitigation: 1) raise upstream_flush_timeout per-route; 2) apply tenant-level concurrency cap (max concurrent streams 30) + soft queuing. That should prevent head-of-line resource exhaustion.

lindsey_pm: what's the UI/console change cadence? Customer wants a patch now. Do we have a way to set a per-tenant edge override quickly?

ash_prodeng: yes we can add a per-route Envoy config via the edge control plane. I'll stage a change: set `upstream_flush_timeout=20s` and `max_concurrent_streams=30` for route `/v1/embeddings:batch` when tenant=acme-corp. I'll run it as a small rollout and watch metrics.

opsbot: Ops action: created change request CR-7783, target rollout window 18:30 UTC.

mike_supp: customer applied reduced batch earlier and is OK to test config change. They asked if we can keep metadata header but compress it or move to body. Any quick guidance?

ash_prodeng: recommend moving large metadata into request body (as JSON) rather than headers. If headers required, compress with base64+gzip and ensure <=2kb. But best is body.

sophie_sre: executing staged change now (rolling 5% -> 50% -> 100%). Observability: increase in request durations but error rate falling on the 5% nodes. I'll post metrics.

[~10m later]

sophie_sre: 50% rollout done, error rate for acme-corp embeds down from 18% -> 3%. CPU on edge proxies up ~6%. No new GOAWAYs observed on staged nodes.

mike_supp: relayed to customer, they're running a long test and will report. They asked for a postmortem and permanent fix timeline.

lindsey_pm: include recommended product guidance: 1) document header size limits for tenants; 2) add console guardrails & per-tenant concurrency config; 3) update quickstart for embeddings to recommend body metadata for large payloads.

ash_prodeng: agreed. I'll open a follow-up ticket to make the per-route upstream_flush_timeout configurable per-tenant and add a validation to reject headers > 4kb at the edge with a clear 4xx error instead of allowing a 502. Ticket: INF-4121.

javier_support: customer happy with temporary patch. They will roll client changes (move metadata to body) and re-test.

mike_supp: closing loop: keep monitoring for 24h and we'll prepare a short postmortem once stable. Thanks all. :tada:
